mechanism_narrative: The 26.7-point rebound in WORKPLACES from -47.6 at t-2w to -20.9 at t-0w marks the collapse of the New Year holiday trough and the restart of office commuting; restored weekday commuter volume raises incidental retail-and-recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly mean moved from -47.6 at t-2w to -20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is not higher than its trailing 28-day mean when WORKPLACES improves by more than 20 points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has held at or above +11 for three consecutive weeks (14.9, 12.9, 11.1), showing a persistent stay-at-home shift; as long as household time at home stays elevated, discretionary retail-and-recreation trips are deferred and RETAIL_REC falls over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean >= +10 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly means 14.9, 12.9, 11.1 across t-2w, t-1w, t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +10, showing stay-at-home time does not suppress discretionary retail.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneously depressed PARKS (-25.1) and TRANSIT (-29.0) show a broad withdrawal from out-of-home leisure and travel under tightening containment; because retail trips are the marginal residual activity once leisure and transit are suppressed, RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both below -20 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS -25.1 and TRANSIT -29.0 jointly depressed at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its trailing-28-day mean in weeks where PARKS and TRANSIT are both below -20.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, transit avoidance is a faster behavioral response than spending adjustment, so TRANSIT declines lead retail footfall by one to two weeks; the transit series sitting 10 points below its t-3w level predicts a further one-week drop in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -18.6 at t-3w to -29.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with rising case counts
failure_condition: After a week in which TRANSIT is below -25, RETAIL_REC is flat or higher in the following week in the majority of observed episodes.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -8.4 at t-1w to -1.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is not above its trailing 28-day mean after GROCERY_PHARM rebounds by 5 or more points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The 19-point gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-1.1) and RETAIL_REC (-20.1) shows household spending substituting out of discretionary retail into essential provisioning; while that substitution gap stays wider than 15 points, discretionary retail trips keep shrinking and RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC >= 15 points in a given week
failure_condition: When the GROCERY_PHARM-minus-RETAIL_REC gap exceeds 15 points, RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is equal to or above its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: If the post-holiday WORKPLACES rebound stalls and stays below -15 for two consecutive weeks, the office-commuting channel that normally anchors weekday retail footfall is absent, and RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks because no other activity series is recovering.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES -20.9 and TRANSIT -29.0 both still deeply negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its trailing-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES stayed below -15 for two consecutive weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically 14.9, 12.9, 11.1 over t-2w to t-0w
